Title: Redistribution and two different Blood Brother players

Messages.Author: Lönkka
Messages.Body:
Redistribution
Action
+1 stealth action.

[san] This acting vampire gains a blood. Then move any amount of blood and equipment among the Blood Brothers in this circle.
[SAN] As above, and untap this acting vampire.

www.secretlibrary.info/index.php?lib=1596

Just checking that if for some bizarre reason you happen to have two players on the same table playing BB's of the same circle Redistribution works among ALL the BBs in play and not just your own, right?

At least the card doesn't specify this...

The set-up (2 of the same circle in same table) is never going to happen though. RIGHT?

Finnish  Politics!

Damn, should have been aware of that ruling. Me setting fire to the other BB player might have saved me in that tournament round.

Follow-up question:

Does superior Slake the Thirst "see" blood moved to a vampire via Redistribution as "blood gained"?

In other words, say Blood Brother A (capacity 4 with 1 blood) plays Redistribution. He gains 1 blood from Redistribution, and then the player decides to move 2 more blood to him from some other BB of the same circle (FROM ACROSS THE TABLE, MWAHAHA!). Sorry. Anyway, if A plays Slake the Thirst at superior after that, can he give 3 blood to some other BB (of the same circle)?

Slake the Thirst
[Action Modifier] Action Modifier
[Combat] Combat

[Sanguinus] Sanguinus

[san] [COMBAT] Only usable when this vampire gains blood. Choose another ready Blood Brother of the same circle. That vampire gains the same amount of blood from the bank.
[SAN] [ACTION MODIFIER] As above, but usable as an action modifier.

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> PetriWessman wrote:
> Does superior Slake the Thirst "see" blood moved to a vampire via Redistribution as "blood gained"?
>
Yes. It also sees the blood you gain earlier (from the first sentence) as blood gained, and you can play the action modifier then instead if you prefer.

[LSJ 20100203]
>
> LSJ wrote:
> > Jerry plays Redistribution and the action succeeds. I decide to move,
> > say, 2 blood from Larry to Jerry. Jerry then plays Slake the Thirst
> > and chooses Larry. How much blood does Larry get?
> > a) 1 blood.
> > b) 3 blood.
> > c) Either 1 or 2 blood.
> > d) Other.
> c). You can gain 1 blood if you play it when "This acting vampire
> gains a blood". Or you can play it when you "move any amount of blood
> and equipment" to gain 2.
>

> > > 1. Can I move 2 blood from Jerry to Larry, then move the 2 blood back
> > > to Jerry and play Slake the Thirst for 2?

Messages.Author: Boris The Blade
Messages.Body: So how to announce the action? Do you have to declare which minions will be affected?

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> Non-existant user wrote:
> So how to announce the action? Do you have to declare which minions will be affected?
>
That would be consistent with the rulebook:
>
> Rulebook, wrote:
> All details of the action are declared when the action is announced, including the target(s), the cost, the effects, etc.
>
Precedent from Rave suggests that if you lose some of the blood between then and resolution (e.g. paying for an action modifier), you move as much as you can.
[LSJ 20011123]

> LSJ wrote:
> > When you declare an action you ahve to announce all terms. So that means
> > when you're doing a Rave with your vamp with 6 blood you will have to tell
> > in advance how much blood you're going to move and to who, right? And if I
>
> Yes.
>
> > want to move my 6 blood and get blocked and I pay 1 blood to stealth then
> > the action will fizzle as I now inly have 5 blood to move?
>
> No. You move what you can - you choose who gets shorted.
>
In general, cards that appear to target blood counters actually target the vampire they're on, and move as much blood as possible if not. e.g. if you steal 2 blood from the opposing minion and they pay for their strike costing 1 blood, you steal the 1 remaining blood rather than having your strike fizzle.
